The existing lab has 60 PCs across 15 LANs, connected by 12 routers with static IPv4 routes. It uses `kathara/base` and currently has no DNS configuration. The following is a proposed working specification for adding name resolution while preserving the existing topology and addresses.

**DNS design.** Run BIND on the existing `r5` router at `10.16.5.1`, and configure all 60 PCs to use it as their DNS resolver. Serve the requested names from local authoritative zones, with recursion disabled. Keep all existing interfaces, IP addresses, routes and connections unchanged. This central server is a single point of failure, but requires no new device or address.

|---|---|---|

Add these MX records, each with priority 10 and an A record for its mail host:

| Mail domain | Mail host | Machine | IPv4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| company.com | mail.company.com | pc7 | 10.16.2.13 |
| university.edu | mail.university.edu | pc11 | 10.16.3.13 |
| dept.company.com | mail.dept.company.com | pc18 | 10.16.5.12 |
| servizi.ministero.gov | mail.servizi.ministero.gov | pc47 | 10.16.12.13 |

The implementation would add BIND configuration and zone files under `r5/`, start the service from `r5.startup`, and persist resolver settings in each PC’s startup configuration. Checks would cover zone syntax, every A and MX record, resolution from PCs at both ends of the network, and connectivity across existing routes. MX records identify mail receivers; they do not themselves install or configure mail services.

The [Kathara creation skill](</var/folders/84/zz92dr1178v8z_tvd_q2dfw40000gn/T/kathara-aut-9qjy6igy/lab/.codex/skills/kathara-creation/SKILL.md>) explicitly says, “Only start creating files after the user asks to create the scenario starting from the generated prompt.” Please ask me to implement this specification when ready. No files have been changed.
